contents.name: Definition 2.1 with Corollary 2.3 and equations (2.4)-(2.6): cellular basis, cell modules and their triangular multiplication
Proposition 2.7, Lemma 2.8 and equation (2.6): associativity and symmetry of the cell form; the radical is a submodule
Proposition 2.9 and Propositions 2.10-2.12: nondegenerate cell quotients are absolutely irreducible; nonzero cell-module maps force comparability
Theorem 2.13 (Graham-Lehrer): the nonzero cell heads are a complete set of pairwise non-isomorphic simple modules
Corollary 2.14: unitriangularity of the decomposition matrix in the cell order
Example 2.2(ii): the explicit cellular basis of H_{R,q}(S_3)
Note 4 after Chapter 2 (dual cellular bases and symmetric algebras)
contents.reason: The note discusses Morita-invariance and dual cellular bases under extra symmetry hypotheses; the page never needs a dual cellular basis, so building it would add inventory with no consumer.

contents.name: Chapter 3 Lemma 3.2, Proposition 3.3 and Corollary 3.4: row standard tableaux, distinguished coset representatives and the basis of the permutation module

Theorem 3.18 (Murphy Basis Theorem) with its $m_{st}^*=m_{ts}$ symmetry

Theorem 3.21 (Dipper-James): the cell heads of the Hecke algebra form the complete list of irreducible modules
Corollary 3.22 (Hoefsmit): split semisimplicity of H_{C(q),q}
Example 3.23: the elements L_1,...,L_4
Proposition 3.24 and Corollary 3.25: the L_k commute and symmetric polynomials in them are central
Lemma 3.26, Lemma 3.27 and Lemma 3.31 (induction step and Garnir relation for the triangular action)
Example 3.29: e-residues for e=3, lambda=(4,2)

Lemma 3.35, Lemma 3.37, Lemma 3.38 and Theorem 3.39: nonvanishing of D^lambda exactly for e-restricted partitions, with dominance unitriangularity
Corollary 3.40: H is split semisimple if and only if e>n
Corollary 3.41: a partition is e-restricted if and only if an e-restricted tableau exists
contents.reason: A purely combinatorial existence statement about e-restricted tableaux; the classification theorem and its dominance corollary do not cite it, so it is not scaffolded on this pair.

contents.name: Chapter 4 (4.1), Theorem 4.8 and Corollaries 4.9, 4.12: the definition of S(d,n), the Hom-bases and the q-permutation modules

Corollary 4.18: dominance unitriangularity of the q-Schur decomposition matrix
Corollary 4.17 (Parshall-Wang): S(d,n) is quasi-hereditary
contents.reason: Quasi-hereditary algebra theory is a separate track topic with no consumer on this page; the triangularity it packages is already stated directly as Corollary 4.18.

contents.name: Proposition 4.19 and Chapter 4 section 3: the Schur idempotent, the corner H = e S(d,n) e and the Schur functor on Weyl and simple modules
Theorem 4.20: the double centralizer property of the q-Schur algebra
contents.reason: The double centralizer is invoked in the source only in the block classification of Chapter 5 section 3, which is scaffolded on the cores-and-blocks page.

contents.name: Chapter 5 Theorem 5.18 and Corollary 5.19: norms of the orthogonalised semistandard basis and G = q^N g
Example 5.20 and Example 5.25: worked Gram determinants for (3,2)
(5.21), (5.22), Lemma 5.23, Proposition 5.24 and Lemma 5.26: beta numbers, signed semistandard multiplicities and the hook-indexed evaluation
Theorem 5.27 (James-Mathas): the weight-space Gram determinant as a hook product
Example 5.28: the G determinant for lambda=(3,2)
Lemma 5.29 (Jantzen): the Gram determinant valuation is the sum of the positive Jantzen layer dimensions
Lemma 5.30: semistandard weight dimensions detect virtual Weyl classes
Theorem 5.31 (Jantzen sum formula) and Corollary 5.32 (q-Schaper)
Example 5.33: the (3,2) calculation at q=-1 and the final d=1 only after the extra dimension argument
Chapter 5 section 3, Lemmas 5.34-5.35, Theorems 5.36-5.37 and Propositions 5.38-5.40: e-core block classification, weight-one matrices and the irreducibility criterion
contents.reason: The e-core/abacus block theory belongs to the planned page cores-quotients-and-blocks-of-symmetric-groups (batch 21 of this run); the weight-one and irreducibility statements are stated there in the convention-translated form required by the gap ledger.

contents.name: Chapter 5 closing discussion before Theorem 5.40: general decomposition numbers and irreducible Specht modules are open
Chapter 6 and the appendices of the 1999 AMS edition (canonical bases, adjustment matrices, modular branching)
contents.reason: These chapters are not part of the retrieved 1998 manuscript; the edition boundary is recorded and no statement from the unseen AMS Chapter 6 is used as evidence anywhere on this pair.

Theorem 3.13 with (3.14)-(3.15): existence, orthogonality, uniqueness and the idempotents of the seminormal basis attached to a coefficient system
Sections 2.2-2.4 and 3.2 (arXiv pp. 6-13 and 18-22): the cyclotomic Hecke-algebra presentation, its JM elements y_r and the cyclotomic generalisation of the seminormal form
contents.reason: This pair needs only the type-A Hecke algebra, whose Murphy basis and JM triangularity are already sourced from Mathas's book; the cyclotomic and quiver-Hecke material is not part of this page's scope.
